reasons.text: Electricity bought is only 0.42x the minimum needed for the tonnes claimed (125 kWh/t against at least 300)
28% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
48% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
100% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.31x the cost floor)
67% of high-value consignments have no e-way bill
Certificates sold at 0.32x the market median price

inspection_checklist: Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
